# Exact local SQLite contract
schema.sql creates one control row id=1 with durable epoch, and one document row id=1 with text value and revision. A separately authorized controller advances control.epoch, monotonically, in the same database before cutover. Client input must never advance it.
write_value(conn, epoch, expected_revision, value) returns True exactly when the supplied epoch equals current control.epoch AND expected_revision equals current document.revision at the write. It then replaces value and increments revision by one atomically. Otherwise returns False and leaves all stored fields unchanged. Valid calls supply positive integer epochs, nonnegative integer revisions and text. Tests need not add other input contracts. Own and finish the operation transaction; connections have no ambient transaction when called. An exception rolls back owned work and propagates. Schema and checker are immutable. Concurrent or direct SQL bypass protection beyond this function is not claimed by this exercise. Reopening the database must preserve current epoch and successful data. Test against real disposable SQLite, not a mock.

def write_value(conn, epoch, expected_revision, value):
    with conn:
        result=conn.execute("UPDATE document SET value=?, revision=revision+1 WHERE id=1 AND revision=? AND ?=(SELECT epoch FROM control WHERE id=1)",(value,expected_revision,epoch))
